text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Cambodia's Second Prime Minister Hun Sen appears to be in firm control of the capital Phnom Penh but his rival Prince Norodon Ranariddh, now in France, vows to organise resistance.
- Singapore construction manager Bryan Ghana saw massive troop movements in Phnom Penh last weekend and returned to Singapore with four other Singaporean workers.
- Indonesian announces slew of deregulation measures, cutting tariffs on 1,600 items as well as curbing land speculation and powers of regional officials to collect special payments from businesses.
- Singapore's anaemic manufacturing sector suffers another decline as output in May slips 1.6 percent year-on-year, led by dip in electronics production.
- Almost all Singapore's adult workers have Post Office Savings Bank accounts, but their balances average relatively low Singapore $8,000 or S$9,000 each.
- Tax exemption granted to POSBank depositors on interest earned has become less attractive since introduction of Goods and Services Tax in April 1994.
- Credit POSB, savings bank's investment arm, continues to retain largest share of housing loans market despite talk it is losing ground in fierce competition with commercial banks.
- Indonesian central bank announces stiff measures to cool property sector including outright ban on new bank credit for land acquisition.
- QAF Ltd's share price shoots up in stock market amid speculation its controlling Indonesian shareholder plans to inject several businesses into Singapore food group.
- DBS Bank strikes deal to take controlling stake in Sri Dhana Finance Public Co Ltd, with aim of creating "super" finance company and ultimately acquiring banking licence.
- Stamford Tyres receives interim payment from its insurers for losses sustained in fire that razed one of its four warehouses recently.
- Engineering and infrastructure group Van Der Horst has secured S$108 million worth of contracts for an oil pipeline project in Sanggaran, Bali, Indonesia.
- Scotts Holdings responds to last week's censure of three of its directors by Stock Exchange of Singapore, stating it recognises need to safeguard interests of all its shareholders.
